newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City smog alert forces cars off roads.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City smog alert forces cars off roads.

text.p: Thick smog choked Mexico City on Thursday, prompting the city government to extend an emergency plan that orders nearly half the city's 3.5 million cars off the road for the third day in a row.
The "two days without a car" programme was enacted on Wednesday when levels of ozone rose to nearly three times the allowable limits, said Ana Cecilia Samper, a city spokeswoman.

On Thursday ozone levels rose to above 200 points on the local IMECA scale. The World Health Organisation says exposure to ozone levels above 100 points for more than an hour per year is dangerous to human health.
"The programme will continue tomorrow (Friday)," Samper told Reuters, adding that this is the third time the plan has been implemented this year.

Ozone is a pollutant that results when car fumes mix with radiation from the sun. In Mexico City, air pollution is made worse by solar radiation at an elevation of more than 7,400 feet (2,250 meters) and mountains that surround the Mexico City Valley, trapping foul air.

Under normal circumstances all cars are banned from city streets one day a week. When the ozone index tops 250, cars are banned two weekdays and one weekend day, depending on their license plate numbers.
